One-pot multi-step cascade protocols toward
β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amides via intermolecular
trapping of an α-indolylpalladium complex by CO †
Huahua Liu, Li Wei and Zhiyuan Chen
 *
Various β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amides were e ﬃciently prepared
from ortho-iodoanilines, propargyl bromides, 1 atm of CO, and
substituted NH-sulfoximines, through a palladium-catalyzed
indole annulation/carbonyl insertion/C –N bond formation
cascade. Mostly good to high yields of the products were obtained
through this multi-step, one-pot reaction protocol under very
gentle reaction conditions. The obtained β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl
amides could be converted into biologically interesting sulfoxi-
mine analogues that contain a tryptamine moiety.
Introduction
Sulfoximines represent an important class of structural motifs
that are found in natural products, pharmaceuticals and agro-
chemicals.1 Some typical sulfoximine-containing molecules,
such as Suloxifen from Gödecke GmbH, 2 pan-CDK inhibitor
Roniciclib (BAY 1000394) from Bayer, 3 and AZD6738 from
AstraZeneca,4 have found important medicinal applications in
practical areas (Fig. 1). In a recent study, Sirvent and Lücking
from Bayer evaluated sulfoximine analogues as an isostere for
amines by incorporation into marketed drugs and advanced
clinical candidates with comparison of the biological pro-
perties.
5 Bolm and co-workers demonstrated the chemical
degradation transformations in the laboratory leading to sul-
foximine degradations.
6 Besides, sulfoximines can also act as
directing groups in C –H activations,7 or as chiral auxiliaries or
ligands in transition-metal mediated asymmetric catalysis. 8
Due to these reasons, studies on the synthetic developments of
sulfoximine chemistry have aroused widespread interest in the
past few decades. 1 On the other hand, the tryptamine sca ﬀold,
possessing an ethanamine moiety at the C-3 position of
indole,9 was recognized as a “privileged structure ” that has
been found in psychoactive compounds like serotonin and
amphetamine (Fig. 1). 10 Compounds bearing a 3-(2-amino-
ethyl)-1H-indole moiety usually exhibit a high agonist action at
multiple receptors.11 Therefore, attempts to construct diversely
functionalized tryptamine libraries proved to be interesting in
drug development or in medicinal research. 12 We envisioned
that the installation of a sulfoximine moiety at the N terminus
of the tryptamine sca ﬀold to form β-indoly sulfoximidoyl
amide A should be beneficial for subsequent biological assays
(Fig. 1).
Synthetic approaches toward functionalized sulfoximines
usually start from free NH-sulfoximines. To date, divergent
transformations of the sulfoximine N –H bond have enabled
N–C bond formation reactions via versatile synthetic methods,
including alkylation, 13 vinylation,14 alkynylation,15 arylation,16
propargylation,17 and cyanation.18 However, these methods are
not applicable for the rapid production of acylated sulfoxi-
mines. N-Acylation of sulfoximines is generally performed by

the reaction of NH-sulfoximines with carboxylic acids or acid
halides.19 Moreover, oxidative coupling reactions of alde-
hydes20 or methyl arenes 21 also o ﬀered alternative strategies
toward these α-ketoamides. Despite such fruitful approaches
being reported, the use of specific types of substrates, such as
carbonyl compounds, is generally necessary. Thus, the devel-
opment of a general synthetic method from readily available
precursors is convenient and thus much valuable.
We recently reported a facile synthesis of fused aza-hetero-
cyclic amides via a palladium-catalyzed intermolecular cascade
reaction of N-aryl-N-allenamides with isocyanides
(Scheme 1).
22 The success of this reaction relies on a direct
trapping of an α-indolylpalladium complex by isocyanide, fol-
lowed by β-H elimination to produce a key ketenimination
intermediate.23 In line with this result and our interest in
sulfoximines,7c,d,24 we wondered whether the
α-indolylpalladium complex species could be e ﬃciently
trapped by CO (carbon monoxide) as a C1 building block, thus
oﬀering an opportunity to construct biologically interesting
β-indoly sulfoximidoyl amides through a multicomponent syn-
thetic strategy.
25
It should be noted that multicomponent reactions (MCRs)
have become powerful aza-heterocyclic synthesizing methods
in designing new heterocyclic sca ﬀolds and regulating medic-
inal or biological properties. 26 Compared with conventional
step-wise reactions, MCRs can provide a simpler procedure to
construct diverse molecules from three or more raw materials
in a one-pot procedure, featuring the advantages of simple
operation, avoidance of wastage of energy and time, and
environmental benignity.
Results and discussion
Our proposed retro-synthetic strategy is presented in
Scheme 2, eqn (1). In this approach, a base-assisted coupling
reaction of ortho-halide aniline 1 with propargyl halide 2 could
be expected to form the ortho-halide substituted
N-allenylaniline intermediate F, which could undergo a regio-
selective 1,2-addition reaction to produce the α-indolyl palla-
dium complex E and D. The species D could be reactive
enough to be trapped by CO to form ArCOPdX species C,
which may undergo β-H elimination to deliver species B. The
following nucleophilic addition reaction of B with NH-sulfoxi-
mine 3 should be able to produce the desired β-indolyl sulfoxi-
midoyl amide A. Nevertheless, two challenges must be met: (1)
a suitable ligand should be provided to facilitate the trapping
of the α-indolylpalladium species with 1 atm of CO under
heterogeneous conditions and (2) due to the weak nucleophilic
ability of the NH-sulfoximines, a strong base might be capable
of boosting β-H elimination to produce the ethenone species,
thus favoring the nucleophilic addition step to form the
expected C –N bond. Stimulated by the aforementioned chal-
lenges, we herein wish to discuss a convenient synthesis of
β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amides from a Pd-catalyzed four-com-
ponent reaction of 2-iodoaniline 1, propargyl bromide 2,
carbon monoxide and NH-sulfoximine 3 [Scheme 2, eqn (2)].
This multi-step, one-pot cascade reaction proceeds smoothly
through the formation of four new chemical bonds in overall
good to excellent yields with excellent functional group toler-
ance under gentle conditions.
To identify the suitable conditions for the proposed Pd-
catalyzed sequential domino process, reaction screening invol-
ving 2-iodoaniline 1a and propargyl bromide 2a as the starting
materials was carried out in various bases and solvents. It was
found from the initial steps I and II that the intermediate
N-allenyl-N-tosyl-2-iodoaniline (F in Scheme 2) was necessary
and crucial for the success of this reaction, because without
the formation of F, the desired product 4a was produced in
only low to modest yields during the screening of the reac-
tions. However, with the addition of tBuOK, N-allenyl-N-tosyl-
2-iodoaniline could be successfully produced in an almost
quantitative yield. Hence, with the perfect generation this
intermediate, the next screening of the Pd-catalyzed conditions
to e ﬃ
ciently generate the final product 4a became feasible.
With this promising result in hand, we next screened the
optimal conditions in step III for further reactions with CO
(balloon) and NH-sulfoximine 3a in the presence of Pd(OAc)
2,
ligand, base and solvent in a one-pot reaction protocol. By uti-
lizing PPh
3 as the ligand, the base was first examined and the
results are presented in Table 1. Initial attempts to employ the
organic bases pyridine or triethylamine only led to complex
results (entries 1 and 2). It was a delight to observe that when
K
2CO3 was used as a base, the desired product 4a could be iso-

lated in 27% yield (entry 3). Based on this experiment, we sub-
sequently screened various Pd catalysts, which again demon-
strated that Pd(OAc) 2 was an optimal Pd catalyst (entries 4 –7).
Other inorganic bases, such as Cs 2CO3 and K 3PO4, were found
to be workable for this reaction to produce the desired product
4a, albeit in poor yields (entries 8 and 9).
With tBuOK as the base in toluene, the product 4a was deli-
vered in 40% yield, whilst an inferior result was observed when
THF, which was employed as the solvent in the previous step
II, was employed in place of toluene (entries 10 and 11). To
our delight, a strong organic base, DBU, was found to be the
optimal base for this reaction. A smooth conversion was
observed and the product 4a was isolated in 94% yield when
DBU was added (entry 12). Another strong organic base
DABCO was not e ﬀective (entry 13); hence, we used DBU for
further optimizations.
Encouraged by these results, we further examined the phos-
phine ligand. The results indicated that electron-rich P ligands
were all e ﬀective for the reaction, whereas PPh
3 again proved
to be the optimal choice (entries 14 –19). For the solvent e ﬀect
in this reaction, carrying out the reaction in THF, 1,4-dioxane,
and DMF did not facilitate the formation of 4a, respectively
(entries 20–22). An identical 92% yield of 4a was obtained with
CH3CN as the solvent (entry 23). Finally, we tried the mixture
solvent of THF : toluene = 1 : 2; however, no satisfactory result
was observed (entry 24). Instead of using the toxic gas CO, we
used Mn(CO)
5Br (1.0 equiv.) as a carbonyl source under N 2,
and the desired product 4a could be isolated in 66% yield
(entry 25).
With the optimized conditions in hand (Table 1, entry 12),
we next studied the scope of this Pd-catalyzed multicomponent
cascade annulation reaction (Scheme 3). The Pd-catalyzed one-
pot reactions of various N-Ts protected 2-iodoanilines 1 with
propargyl bromide 2a, NH-sulfoximine 3a and 1 atm of CO
were firstly evaluated. As shown in Scheme 2, a broad range of
β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amides 4 could be readily obtained.
The ortho-iodoanilines 1 with electron-donating groups at the
para-( 4c and 4d)o r meta-positions ( 4g) of the phenyl moiety
all delivered the corresponding products in good yields. The
electron-withdrawing halide substituents, such as F ( 4e, 4h
and 4k) and Cl ( 4b, 4f, and 4i), on the phenyl moiety could
aﬀord the corresponding products in good to high yields.

Gratifyingly, the synthetically useful bromide atom could also
be tolerated under these Pd-catalyzed conditions, delivering
the desired products 4j and 4p in 70% and 86% yields, respect-
ively. In addition, non-terminal propargyl bromides 2 turned
out to be suitable starting materials as well; R 2 and R 3 could
be a methyl or phenyl group, thus leading to poly-substituted
β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amides 4l and 4m in acceptable yields.
The variations on the S-linkage of NH-sulfoximines 3 were
further studied under the Pd-catalyzed one-pot reaction con-
ditions. For the S-methyl substituted aryl NH-sulfoximines,
various substitutions on the benzene ring at di ﬀerent posi-
tions with varied electronic natures were readily allowed,
leading to the desired products 4n–4r with good to excellent
eﬃciency. The halide substituents attached at the phenyl ring
could be Cl ( 4o, 4r)o rB r( 4p), showing their further synthetic
potential through Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions
with organometallic agents. Except for the S-methyl group in
substrate 3a, other alkyl groups that were linked at the S atom
in substrates 3 were also divergent, including ethyl ( 4s), steri-
cally hindered cyclopropyl ( 4t) and benzyl ( 4u) groups.
NH-Sulfoximine 3 that contains an S-naphthyl group under-
went the reaction smoothly to give product 4v in 92% yield.
Diphenyl NH-sulfoximine was a viable substrate, leading to the
corresponding products 4w and 4y in good yields, respectively.
The structure of compound 4w was established unambigu-
ously by X-ray crystal di ﬀraction analysis.
27 In addition to the
results, the benzoylphenone derivative 4z (74% yield) showed
the compatible property of ketone substitutions.
Having demonstrated a broad reaction scope obtained
using Ts-protected ortho-iodoaniline 1 as the key substrate, our
attention turned to the easily removable protecting groups
which were linked at the indole N moieties. It was found that
this reaction did not work with an acyl-protected compound,
N-(2-iodophenyl)acetamide, with propargyl bromide 2a,C O( 1
atm) and NH-sulfoximine 3a under the Pd-catalyzed con-
ditions. Meanwhile, only a moderate yield of acetyl protected
indole 6a was obtained in the Pd-catalyzed three-component
tandem annulation reaction of N-(2-iodophenyl)-N-( prop-2-yn-
1-yl)acetamide 5 with 1 atm of CO and NH-sulfoximine 3a
(Scheme 4). However, the situation could be significantly
changed when N-aryl-N-allenamide 7 was employed as a useful
substrate with 1 atm of CO and NH-sulfoximine 3a under the
Pd-catalyzed conditions (Scheme 4). For this approach, the
starting materials acyl-protected N-allenamide 7 and 3a were
mixed in toluene at room temperature; then Pd(OAc)
2/PPh3
and DBU were added under a CO balloon atmosphere. To our
delight, the Ac-protected indole 6a was successfully formed in
84% yield. The reaction of Boc-protected N-allenamide 7 and
3a with CO was also compatible under the Pd-catalyzed con-
ditions, a ﬀording the desired Boc-protected indoles 6b–6e in
good to excellent yields. Unfortunately, for the H- or alkyl-sub-
stituted substrates 7, no desired product 6f was isolated
(Scheme 5).
A gram-scale reaction of Ts-protected N-allenamide 7a with
NH-sulfoximine 3a under a CO balloon atmosphere a ﬀorded
the desired β-indolyl acetyl amide 4a in 86% yield (Scheme 6,
eqn (1)). The products prepared by this procedure are valuable
precursors for the synthesis of biologically interesting sulfoxi-
mine analogues that contain a tryptamine moiety. For
instance, compound 4a could be readily reduced by BH
3·Me2S
in dichloromethane to a ﬀord a tryptamine derivate 8 in 65%
yield (Scheme 6, eqn (2)). Considering the importance of the
tryptamine and sulfoximine structural motifs as pharma-
ceutical candidates (Fig. 1), we hope that the resulting product
8 should be able to exhibit potential biological or medicinal
activities in future medicinal studies.

Conclusions
In summary, we have described a room temperature Pd-cata-
lyzed multi-step one-pot cascade reaction of ortho-iodoaniline,
propargyl bromide, 1 atm of CO and NH-sulfoximine, which
enables operational convenience toward β-indolyl sulfoximi-
doyl amides in mostly good to excellent yields under carefully
modified reaction conditions. The success of this reaction
was attributed to the intermolecular trapping of an
α-indolylpalladium complex by CO. Because the obtained pro-
ducts could be potential biologically active sulfoximine deriva-
tives that contain a tryptamine moiety, the variability of the
starting materials and their easy accessibility make this proto-
col extremely attractive. Protecting groups such as Ac and Boc
located at the indole N atom could be compatible for the reac-
tions of N-aryl-N-allenamide with CO and NH-sulfoximine.
Considering the easy availability of the starting materials and
the gentle but highly e ﬃcient catalytic systems, this one-pot
synthetic protocol could serve as a valuable and powerful
method for the expedient synthesis of biologically active
compounds.
Experimental section
General procedure for the synthesis of β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl
amide 4a
Step I: To a stirred solution of 2-iodoaniline 28 1a (164 mg,
0.44 mmol) and K 2CO3 (60.72 mg, 0.44 mmol) in 1.0 mL of
acetone was added 3-bromoprop-1-yne 2a (45 μl, 1.2 mmol) at
room temperature under a N 2 atmosphere. The resulting solu-
tion was stirred at 60 °C for 1 hour. Upon completion of this
reaction as monitored by TLC, acetone was removed using a
rotary evaporator.
Step II: Following the first step I, anhydrous THF (1.0 mL)
was added into the flask under a nitrogen atmosphere; the
solution was cooled to 0 °C, and then tBuOK in THF (0.5 mL)
was added dropwise (64.6 mg, 0.56 mmol). The reaction
mixture was stirred, allowed to warm to room temperature and
stirred for an additional 1 hour. A light yellow solution was
obtained in this step. Upon the disappearance of the key inter-
mediate as monitored via TLC, the solvent THF was removed
using a rotary evaporator to give a crude residue, which was
used in the next step without purification.
Step III: Following step II, Pd(OAc)
2 (4.48 mg, 5 mol%),
PPh3 (20.96 mg, 20 mol%), DBU (121.8 mg, 0.80 mmol), NH-
sulfoximine 3a (62.0 mg, 0.40 mmol), and dry toluene (2.0 mL)
were added sequentially. The resulting brown solution was
purged with a CO balloon 3 times, and then stirred at room
temperature for 2 –3 h. A yellow solution was obtained. Upon
completion of the reaction as indicated by TLC, the reaction
mixture was filtered through a short pad of silica gel and
washed with ethyl acetate (15.0 mL) unless otherwise noted.
The concentration of the filtrate under reduced pressure pro-
vided a crude product, which was purified by silica gel column
chromatography ( petroleum ether/ethyl acetate = 10 : 1 –3:1 ,
v/v) to a ﬀord the desired compound 4a as a white solid.
The other products 4b to 4y were prepared through a
similar procedure to that of product 4a.

General procedure for the gram-scale synthesis of 4a
A screw capped Schlenk tube equipped with a stir bar was
charged with N-(2-iodophenyl)-4-methyl-N-( propa-1,2-dien-1-
yl)benzenesulfonamide 7a (987.0 mg, 2.4 mmol), NH-sulfoxi-
mine 3a (310 mg, 2.0 mmol), Pd(OAc) 2 (0.1 mmol, 5 mol%),
PPh3 (0.4 mmol, 20 mol%), DBU (4.0 mmol), and dry toluene
(10 mL). The reaction mixture was purged with a CO balloon 3
times, and then stirred at room temperature for 6 h. The reac-
tion was monitored by TLC. Upon completion of the reaction,
the reaction mixture was filtered through a short pad of silica
gel and the solid residue was washed with ethyl acetate
(∼15 mL). The concentration of the filtrate under reduced
pressure provided the crude product, which was purified by
silica gel column chromatography ( petroleum ether/ethyl
acetate = 10 : 1 –3 : 1, v/v) to a ﬀord the desired compound 4a,
801 mg, 86% yield.
General procedure for the preparation of compound 8
To an ice cold stirred solution of β-indolyl sulfoximidoyl amide
4a (0.3 mmol) in freshly distilled CH
2Cl2 (3.0 mL) was added
dropwise the borane complex (3.0 equiv.) under a N 2 atmo-
sphere. After stirring for 3 h at 0 °C, the ice bath was removed
and the mixture was warmed to r.t. The reaction mixture was
stirred at room temperature overnight. Upon completion of the
reaction as monitored by TLC, the reaction was carefully
quenched with MeOH and H
2O, and the resulting mixture was
extracted with CH 2Cl2. The combined organic extracts were
dried over MgSO 4, and the solvent was evaporated under
reduced pressure. The crude residue was purified through
silica gel chromatography to yield the pure product 7 as a
white solid in 65% yield.
